foundations.themeContract: System, light, and dark are resolved exclusively by ThemeProvider. Components read semantic colors through useTheme().
foundations.colorsContract: Screens choose a semantic role. Product areas use accent domains instead of random hex values.
foundations.canonicalPalette: Canonical Fam palette: light and dark
foundations.typographyContract: Font size, line height, and default weight come from one Txt variant. Tone describes meaning, not decoration.
foundations.sampleText: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
foundations.tokensContract: Repeated measurements come from tokens. Layout uses native StyleSheets; dynamic colors come from the theme.
foundations.tokensSource: index.ts: space, radius, font, and responsive values
foundations.themeChanges: Changes fully with the active theme.

components.surfacesContract: Surface defines only a semantic background role. Card groups related content. Pure layout remains a View.
components.cardsProgress: Cards with shadows and progress rings
components.noShadowCode: Every surface stays without a shadow. There is no local shadow geometry or shadow color.
components.retryConnection: Try again or check the connection.
components.foundationDescription: Card, Spacer, and Divider from the foundation API.
components.semanticPurpose: One semantic surface, one clear purpose.
components.buttonsControlsContract: Product screens use feature-facing components. Variants express meaning; sizes and 3D depth are not rebuilt per screen.
components.modalCode: RN modal remains limited to justified center/fullscreen/system special cases. The iOS reference uses a SwiftUI BottomSheet with controlled isPresented state and native detents for content flow. ConfirmationDialog is native action-sheet semantics with cancel and destructive roles.
components.settingsCode:
Custom: icon tiles, dividers, and theme colors (settings-menu.tsx), visually identical on iOS and Android with full row control.
Expo UI: FieldGroup renders a real SwiftUI Form (iOS) or Compose LazyColumn (Android) with native look and feel. Chevron uses Icon.select (SF Symbol on iOS, @expo/material-symbols XML on Android) instead of an emoji tile; each row is a native node on the JS thread, not virtualized, and is intended only for short fixed lists such as settings menus.
components.shortConfirmations: For short confirmations and focused interactions.
components.sheetDescription: Modal(transparent, slide) + Pressable backdrop + handle bar.
components.nativeHeights: Detail content with native iOS heights.
components.feedbackContract: Success, warning, and error use semantic tones. Loading, empty, and progress states make the state and next step visible.
components.feedbackSource: Txt tones, progress components, and EmptyState
components.adjustSearch: Adjust the search term or add a product.
components.pressedHint: While held, the button should become noticeably smaller and more transparent.
components.webHint: The native Expo UI examples are available on iOS and Android.

patterns.screensContract: Screen owns safe area, background, content width, scrolling, and header. chrome is for main areas, back is for subpages.
patterns.screenBehavior: The real screen handles safe area and scrolling outside this preview.
patterns.headerRoles: Navigation, title, and action stay in fixed roles.
patterns.chromeRule:
Never combine chrome and back.
Fallback target: back={{ label: 'Pantry', href: '/fridge' }}
patterns.hybridContract: Static layout, theme values, calculated measurements, native special values, and foreign components use typed styles.
patterns.rule1: Is the value static? Use centralized layout styles.
patterns.rule2: Does the value come from the theme or data? Use style or useThemedStyles().
patterns.rule3: Does the semantics repeat? Centralize it as a token or component.
patterns.accessibilityContract: Interactive elements have a role, clear label, at least a 44-point target, and a visible state that is not conveyed by color alone.
patterns.accessibilitySource: UI contracts and React Native accessibility
patterns.readable: Txt combines font size and line height so content remains readable with larger system settings.

reanimated.title: Reanimated and worklets
reanimated.contract: Animations and gestures stay transient. Calculations run on the UI thread while domain state changes are deliberately scheduled back to React Native.
reanimated.motionHint: One-shot feedback stays on the UI thread and responds directly to a user action.
reanimated.reducedMotion: Reduced Motion is active: time-based transitions are shortened.
reanimated.gestureHint: Gesture values are processed on the UI thread. Only the domain result returns to React Native.
reanimated.derivedHint: One progress value controls several UI properties. The derivation stays on the UI thread and does not create a React render per frame.
reanimated.compositionHint: Static theme-dependent styles and dynamic animated styles are combined as an array.
reanimated.spreadHint: Animated styles can lose their runtime values this way.
reanimated.useSharedValue: UI-thread values without a React render.
reanimated.useAnimatedStyle: Connects shared values to dynamic view styles.
reanimated.useDerivedValue: Derives UI-thread values without JS state.
reanimated.gesturePan: Direct values for drag, swipe, and reorder interactions.
reanimated.scheduleOnRn: Schedules domain results back to the RN thread.
reanimated.useCasesHint: These patterns fit interactions already used in the product or suitable for extension.
reanimated.pressFeedbackHint: Buttons, FABs, and icons provide immediate feedback through spring and timing animations.
reanimated.dragDropHint: The weekly plan processes drag movement on the UI thread and reports only the drop to React Native.
reanimated.swipeActionsHint: Inventory rows can reveal actions such as completing or deleting with a controlled gesture.
reanimated.focusedTransitionsHint: Drawer, jiggle, and celebration interactions stay event-driven and are not continuously redrawn.
